request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
Sheets in the same tree now share one claim number sequence, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works now:** when a claim is opened, it gets one more than the highest number already given on any sheet in its tree. The tree is found by following parent links up to the top sheet (stopping if a sheet comes up twice), then taking every sheet below it. Numbers already given are not changed. Period numbering (`P1-1`, `X-1`, …) is still counted per sheet.

**Changes (server only — no schema, front-end or audit changes were needed):**
- `sheet/SheetRepository.java`: a new `tree(id)` method returns the top sheet followed by all the sheets below it.
- `claim/ClaimRepository.java`: `nextNumber` now takes the tree. It locks the top sheet's row first, so two claims opened at the same moment anywhere in the tree can't get the same number. It then sets this sheet's last number to the tree's highest plus one, in a single update.
- `claim/ClaimNumbers.java`: passes the tree to `nextNumber`. This one function is used by open, bulk open, split, reassign, transfer and clone, so they all use the shared sequence.

**Two behaviours to be aware of:**
- **Re-parenting:** the tree is worked out fresh each time a claim is opened. If a sheet moves to a different tree, its next number follows the highest number in the new tree, even if that is lower than numbers it gave before. Numbers can then repeat across sheets that were once in the same tree. The tests don't cover moving a sheet.
- **Locking:** if the top of the tree changes while two claims are being opened (because a parent setting changes at the same moment), the lock on the old top sheet no longer guards the new tree, so two claims could get the same number.
